title: Longest-element duality for finite-root-system subword containment
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a positive definite symmetric bilinear form $(\ ,\ )$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Let $\Phi\subseteq V\setminus\{0\}$ be a finite spanning reduced crystallographic root system: $\Phi\cap\mathbf R\alpha=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$, each reflection $s_\alpha(v)=v-2(v,\alpha)(\alpha,\alpha)^{-1}\alpha$ permutes $\Phi$, and $2(\beta,\alpha)/(\alpha,\alpha)\in\mathbf Z$ for all roots. Fix a base $\Delta\subseteq\Phi$, meaning a vector-space basis for which every root has integer coordinates all nonnegative or all nonpositive, and let $\Phi^+$ be the roots with nonnegative coordinates. Let $W$ be the subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf R}(V)$ generated by the $s_\alpha$, and let $w_0\in W$ satisfy $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$. For $a,b\in W$ write $a\preceq b$ if some reduced word in the simple reflections $\{s_\alpha:\alpha\in\Delta\}$ with product $b$ contains a reduced subword with product $a$; a word is reduced if it has the least possible number of factors. Then $$a\preceq b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w_0b\preceq w_0a.$$ This includes $V=0$, $\Phi=\Delta=\varnothing$, $W=\{1\}$ and $w_0=1$. No geometric flag-variety statement is assumed.

source.place: Brion--Kumar Section 2.1, printed pp.61--63: equation (1), subword description of Bruhat order, and opposite-cell paragraph (conjugation by the longest element reverses the order). Abstract finite-root-system formulation extracted by the agent; the usual exchange argument gives this independently of flag varieties. Primary author-hosted PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-simple-root-reflection-generation], the group $W$ of the statement equals the simple-reflection subgroup $W_\Delta$. Thus its reduced words and lengths are precisely those in the two new inputs. Put $N=\#\Phi^+$. By [lem-sfb-root-length-inversion-count], $\ell(w)$ counts positive roots that $w$ sends negative. Since $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$ and $w_0$ is linear, $w_0(-\Phi^+)=\Phi^+$. Every $w$ permutes $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup(-\Phi^+)$, so $w_0w\beta$ is negative exactly when $w\beta$ is positive. Taking complementary subsets of $\Phi^+$ gives $$\ell(w_0w)=N-\ell(w).$$ The inverse $w_0^{-1}$ also swaps the two root signs, so the identical count gives $\ell(w_0^{-1}w)=N-\ell(w)$ for every $w\in W$.

proof.text: Assume $a\preceq b$. Apply [lem-sfb-root-subword-reflection-chains] to get $a=x_0,\ldots,x_m=b$ with $x_{i+1}=x_i s_{\gamma_i}$ and strictly increasing lengths. Each root reflection is an involution: substituting its formula twice gives $s_{\gamma_i}^2=1$. Define $y_j=w_0x_{m-j}$ for $0\leq j\leq m$. If $i=m-j-1$, then $$y_{j+1}=w_0x_i=w_0x_{i+1}s_{\gamma_i}=y_j s_{\gamma_i},\qquad \ell(y_{j+1})=N-\ell(x_i)>N-\ell(x_{i+1})=\ell(y_j).$$ Thus $y_0=w_0b,\ldots,y_m=w_0a$ is an increasing right-reflection chain. The reverse implication of the same cited criterion gives $w_0b\preceq w_0a$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Proposition 2.3.4 with Corollary 2.3.3, printed p.37; agent-written root-sign complement and explicit reversal of the chains of Definition 2.1.1 and Theorem 2.2.2. University-hosted PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $w_0b\preceq w_0a$ and use [lem-sfb-root-subword-reflection-chains] to choose an increasing chain $z_0=w_0b,\ldots,z_m=w_0a$, with $z_{i+1}=z_i s_{\gamma_i}$. Set $t_j=w_0^{-1}z_{m-j}$. Reversing each edge gives $t_{j+1}=t_j s_{\gamma_{m-j-1}}$, and step 1 gives $\ell(t_{j+1})>\ell(t_j)$. The endpoints are $t_0=a$ and $t_m=b$. Apply the reverse implication of the cited criterion to obtain $a\preceq b$. This argument uses $w_0^{-1}$, so no unproved assertion that $w_0^2=1$ is needed.

source.place: Section 2.3, Proposition 2.3.4 with Corollary 2.3.3, printed p.37; agent-written root-sign complement and explicit reversal of the chains of Definition 2.1.1 and Theorem 2.2.2. University-hosted PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: If $a=b$, both constructions use a chain with $m=0$. In rank zero the spanning assumption gives $V=0$, every generated group here is $\{1\}$, the empty expression is reduced, and $N=0$. Hence the preceding argument includes exactly the asserted empty-root-system case.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q92-5d933eb7b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and both new nodes in full. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to base, and live and side-live still have the item unsplit, so nothing supersedes this delivery. There is no repair note. Step 1 cites generation (W = W_Δ) and the inversion count, and complementing root signs gives ℓ(w₀w) = ℓ(w₀⁻¹w) = N − ℓ(w). I checked the formulas of steps 2 and 3: the chain criterion (i)⇒(ii), then reversing each edge with s_γ² = 1 and multiplying by w₀ or w₀⁻¹, gives the reversed increasing chain, and (ii)⇒(i) closes each direction. The item's ⪯ is literally condition (i) of the chain node. Step 4 (empty chain, rank 0) is genuinely elementary. lem-sfb-root-length-inversion-count (Björner–Brenti Prop 4.4.4) and lem-sfb-root-subword-reflection-chains (Björner–Brenti Def 2.1.1 with Thm 2.2.2, and Prop 4.4.5 for reflections ↔ roots) are true standard theorems. Neither restates the item: neither has w₀ or the order duality. B1–B4 hold, the searches are of all three kinds with real results, and Mathlib has no match: Coxeter has only Basic/Inversion/Length/Matrix, and RootSystem has no length theorem. I found no duplicate in a sweep of all reflection, Weyl, Bruhat and ℓ(w) nodes in sfb and ag (root-sign-word-deletion, chamber-transitivity, bott-samelson, simple-bruhat-double-coset, the parent schubert-closure), nor in a grep of the main-20261015 blueprint. Everything stays in unit sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability, so there are no tool_uses and no cycle. The parent schubert-closure step 7 gets exactly what it needs. Brion–Kumar and Björner–Brenti are not in literature/ (WANTED, proof_origin agent). Milne iAG App. C, which is local, gives only the root/base setup. My own enumeration (A2, B2, G2, A1×A1, A3; 836 ordered pairs in total) confirms the length count, the subword⇔chain equivalence and the item's equivalence. Maintainer note: the item's source.place still says 'conjugation by the longest element reverses the order'. That is wrong: left multiplication reverses it, conjugation preserves it. The report claims to have corrected it, but source is a maintainer field and is unchanged. Please edit it by hand; it does not affect the statement or proof.
